incidents.vector: Exploited SS7 and Diameter signaling protocol flaws in hacked telco infrastructure to plant backdoors and run malicious commands.
incidents.impact: Enabled tracking of subscriber locations and interception of calls and SMS, with covert surveillance of political figures and government officials across six countries.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack against the national ePUAP e-government platform; initial access method still under investigation.
incidents.impact: Poland temporarily suspended the ePUAP portal used for government digital services; officials say evidence points to a foreign adversary.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed port equipment left exposed online, triggering a power outage that cascaded into a wider network compromise.
incidents.impact: Brazil's largest port ran on manual procedures for five days; internet and phone systems have since been partially restored.

incidents.victim: City of Osaka and ~400 Arara email-service customers (incl. Sega)
incidents.vector: Hackers compromised the Arara email distribution platform used by TKC Corporation and other vendors to send mass phishing emails impersonating financial institutions.
incidents.impact: Exposed more than 77 million email addresses across nearly 400 organizations, including 1 million tied to Osaka's administrative services platform.

incidents.vector: A ransomware affiliate breached university systems and claimed the attack.
incidents.impact: Personal information of students and employees was stolen; the MachForms portal remains offline during the investigation.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack encrypted parts of the Belarusian cloud provider's infrastructure; initial access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Disrupted cloud hosting, corporate email, and customer support for businesses across Belarus for several days; no evidence of data theft found.

incidents.vector: Threat actors abused compromised ScreenConnect sessions to silently install unauthorized remote-access clients and deploy the SCKit worm, which hijacks technician sessions to spread to downstream customer endpoints.
incidents.impact: ConnectWise is investigating roughly 400 compromised MSP environments; the worm grants attackers remote administration of affected endpoints.

incidents.victim: Government agencies and critical-sector organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: Open-source AI framework Artex automates reconnaissance through data exfiltration, letting low-skilled operators chain full intrusion phases in hours.
incidents.impact: FBI warns the tool is being used by criminals and nation-states to breach government and critical-infrastructure networks at 'machine speed'; it keeps spreading via forks despite the original repository's removal.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited an Ethereum smart-account (EIP-7702) feature to install a malicious 'sweeper' that drained treasury wallets within minutes of gaining authorization.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen from at least 11 Binance wallets; DOJ and partners have frozen $2.7 billion and obtained court authorization to seize $1.2 billion of it.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor manufacturers, U.S. defense-policy organizations, and civil society groups
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers paired an open-source AI penetration-testing framework with Chinese large language models to autonomously plan and execute intrusions against assigned targets.
incidents.impact: Ten of 19 targeted organizations were compromised, yielding stolen credentials, over a million exposed personal records, military/government identities, and persistent admin access.

incidents.victim: European supermarket chains and food retailers (France and 10+ countries)
incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to internet-exposed refrigeration controllers and forced units into defrost mode, raising temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F).
incidents.impact: French officials attributed the attacks to an IRGC cyber unit; hundreds of supermarkets lost inventory, some units caught fire, and medical-facility refrigeration was also affected.

incidents.victim: Global ransomware victims infected via the Gootloader/StealC/CastleRAT botnet
incidents.vector: Malware distributed through compromised websites sold initial access to ransomware affiliates, while parallel infrastructure ran credential theft and command-and-control.
incidents.impact: International law enforcement dismantled more than 235 servers and 257 domains; DOJ says this malware enabled at least 44 U.S. ransomware attacks costing $29 million since 2018.

incidents.victim: 18 EU politicians, law enforcement officials, and journalists
incidents.vector: Pro-Kremlin hacktivist group published personal information it gathered on high-profile targets.
incidents.impact: Exposed personal data of senior EU and national officials, including Europol's cybercrime chief and journalists who cover Russian influence operations.

incidents.vector: State-linked hackers deployed destructive data-wiping malware after gaining access to the victim's network.
incidents.impact: First known destructive wiping attack by this Belarusian state-linked group, disrupting a company with a key role in Ukraine's transportation sector.

incidents.victim: Li Auto EV owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers hijacked master user accounts on EVs tied to Chinese eSIMs used for vehicle registration, locking owners out of their cars.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed owners lost control of their vehicles and were extorted to regain access; the true number of affected cars is likely higher.

incidents.vector: Extortionists email small developers threatening to use AI tools to clone and publicly release their unreleased or demo games.
incidents.impact: Ransom demands have ranged from hundreds to thousands of dollars; the campaign has driven many developers to pull demos from Steam.
